pr_title: Fix a deadlock in EventSource and CounterGroup
pr_body:
Fix #40190 

A deadlock can occur when the callback encountered in counter.WritePayload() contains a path that contains a EventSource constructor. EventSource constructor tries to take EventSource.EventListenerLock which may already be held by another thread. Simultaneously, the thread that holds to the EventListenerLock can be blocked on s_CounterGroupLock if it calls enable on an EventSource with EventCounter enabled, resulting in a deadlock.

Essentially the only change in this PR is taking out the call to counter.WritePayload(); to out of the scope of s_counterGroupLock. The fields in CounterGroup (both static and non-static) are still read/written inside s_counterGroupLock.

Note: We may need to backport this fix to 3.1.

issue_context.title: Using EventCounter/EventListener can run into a deadlock
issue_context.body:
When EventListener subscribes to EventCounter, it is possible for a deadlock to occur when a callback that tries to invoke EventSource's constructor is registered as the callback for EventListener that's consuming an EventCounter, or if the EventCounter is a PollingCounter/IncrementingPollingCounter and the delegate for polling the value has a call to EventSource's constructor.

Specifically, the problem happens because of two locks:
`EventSource.EventListenersLock` and `CounterGroup.s_counterGroupLock`. 

The polling thread used by CounterGroup to poll and write counter payloads takes the s_counterGroupLock lock and tries to poll the values if it is Polling counter and push out the values. 

The deadlock can occur if either:
1. The delegate for polling value has a call that can invoke EventSource's constructor 
2. The callback registered on the EventListener that listens on the counter value has a call that invokes EventSource's constructor 

Either way, EventSource's constructor tries to take EventSource.EventListenersLock to register itself to the list of known EventListeners. 

Now consider a second thread that's running EventListener.Enable() or EventListener.Disable() on an EventSource that contains counters. Along the way it calls `EventSource.SendCommand` and [takes the EventListenersLock](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/master/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/Diagnostics/Tracing/EventSource.cs#L2553). When the SendCommand callback reaches the call to CounterGroup.OnEventSourceCommand, it tries to take the [s_counterGroupsLock](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/master/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/Diagnostics/Tracing/CounterGroup.cs#L57).

These two threads can then run into a deadlock.

review_comments: ResetCounters() is one of the pieces of functionality that was previously mutually exclusive because of the lock, but now isn't.  What would happen if part way through the below loop, on another thread, we called DisableTimer(), then EnableTimer() which will cause ResetCounters() to run?

I think the methods on the individual counters invoked in ResetCounters() - UpdateMetric() and ResetStatistics() - is protected by the individual counters' lock so I don't think that would mess up the payload that's being written. It is possible for the value of a particular counter that is part of this group to be cleared out, although I don't think that would be a huge issue. Do you think otherwise?
We chatted offline and concluded this fine as-is : )
